tasks.completion_note: Implemented authenticated Capital.com minute OHLC subscriptions for configured epics, bid/ask update normalization, eight-minute WebSocket keepalive, bounded reconnect, and REST backfill beginning at the last observed minute to recover incomplete candles. Forced-disconnect, resubscription, gap-fill, ping, and epic-limit tests pass in GitHub Actions run 37119657855. Ready for Claude review in PR #5. CLAUDE REVIEW 1 (changes requested). Approved as written: epic cap 40, token-bearing messages never logged by this module, 8-minute ping, bounded reconnect backoff, REST backfill from the last observed minute, strict numeric validation, bid and ask both captured, offline tests with forced disconnect. Required changes: (1) Silent-failure risk. Subscribe and ping replies are ignored, so a subscription made with stale session tokens (REST session idle more than 10 minutes) fails without any signal and the socket just sits open. Do all three: (a) call the REST client's ping() before every connection attempt so the tokens are fresh; (b) read the subscribe reply and treat any non-OK status, or any requested epic not confirmed, as a failure that closes the socket and reconnects with a fresh session (log epic names and status only); (c) require a reply to each ping within 30 seconds and treat a missing or non-OK reply as a dead connection. Liveness must rest on ping replies, not on price flow, because markets are legitimately silent when closed. Add tests for stale-token subscribe error, missing ping reply and non-OK ping reply. (2) websockets DEBUG logging prints frames, including the cst and securityToken fields. Force logging.getLogger('websockets') to WARNING at import of this module (and in configure_logging) and add a test that DEBUG records from it cannot be emitted. (3) Exceptions raised inside the on_update callback are currently caught by the generic reconnect handler and look like network errors. Let consumer exceptions propagate out of run_forever (log type only) so a bug in the recorder is visible and supervised, not hidden in a reconnect loop. Add a test. (4) Add scripts/verify_capital_stream.py for the owner to run on the pod: demo-only guard as in verify_capital_demo.py, argument --epic (default US100) and --seconds (default 90), prints redacted JSON only: counts of bid and ask updates, first and last update time, whether ping reply was OK, number of reconnects, and the epic. No tokens, no account data. Document in infra/runpod/README.md that on weekends the owner can pass --epic BTCUSD as a test-only stream (BTCUSD is never added to instruments.yaml and never traded). Live verification on the pod is the acceptance for this task. CODEX REVIEW-CYCLE 1 FIXES: validates REST session before each connection; checks subscribe acknowledgements for OK status and each configured epic; validates immediate and periodic ping acknowledgements with a 30-second timeout; logs websockets at WARNING; logs callback exception type and propagates the original exception; adds the demo-only owner verification script and RunPod instructions. Also addresses automated PR review: naive snapshotTimeUTC is interpreted as UTC and REST gap-fill starts at the earliest side watermark while suppressing per-side duplicates. Full CI run 37120689237 passed (lint, typecheck, migrations, tests, handoff validation, secret scan, Docker/runtime and backup/restore). review_notes: Cycle 2 of 2. V-140 items 1, 2, 3 (re-validate at confirm), 4, 5, 9 and 10 are fixed and verified. Four items remain; fix exactly these, anything new from me after this goes to the owner as a question.

B1 (blocker). Gate settings never reach the real config. strategy_lab.yaml is nested (gate1_backtest_to_paper.min_trades) but _persist writes flat keys such as gate1_min_trades at the top level, so the value is ignored or the strict loader (trader.core.config.load_config_file) rejects the file on restart. Add an explicit key to (file, path) map, using the same names as _check_strategy_floors in core/config.py (gate1_min_trades -> gate1_backtest_to_paper.min_trades and so on; risk keys stay top level in risk.yaml). Also, when the file does not yet exist in /workspace/config, seed the document from the checked-in default in config/ before changing the key (today a missing file is written with a single key, which fails the loader). Test: copy the real config/risk.yaml and config/strategy_lab.yaml into tmp_path, apply one risk change and one gate change through the service, then load them with load_all_configs and assert the new values and that nothing else changed.

B2 (blocker). A scheduled loosening can overwrite a later tightening. Example: loosening 0.5 to 0.75 is scheduled for tomorrow, the owner then tightens to 0.25 today, and apply_due writes 0.75 over it. In apply_due re-validate against the CURRENT value: the stored old_value must equal the current value, and bounds and consistency must still pass; otherwise drop it with an audit entry and a notification. Also refuse a new request for a key that already has a scheduled change, and prune expired pending changes inside request_change (today an expired pending blocks that key with 'already pending' until someone confirms it). Tests for both.

B3 (blocker). Apply is not fully transactional: _persist runs first, then version_store.append; if the store fails, the file is already changed while memory is not. Write the version-store record first or restore the previous file contents when the store fails, and test with a failing store that file and memory both keep the old value.

B4 (blocker, small). halt_active defaults to a callable that always returns False, so a wiring mistake silently disables the halt gate. Make halt_active a required argument (tests pass lambda: False explicitly). Also route revert() through request_change so its refusals are audited.

Non-blocking follow-ups (not required now): declare load_pending/save_pending on the SettingsVersionStore Protocol instead of getattr; add a resolve_startup path for the owner to clear the startup refusal; fsync before the rename; remove leftover temp files on failure.
